evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Core models are covered by tests (uniqueness, freshness, references); errors surface in CI rather than in a management meeting.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: The JD repeatedly emphasizes tests, reviews, documentation, governance, and reliability across the 3/6/12-month plan, with no velocity-oriented shipping-speed language, making this strongly rigour-dominant.
evidence.domain_risk: Board and investor metrics (churn and retention, cohorts, unit economics) can be reproduced from versioned models at any time.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: The role feeds investor and board reporting with GDPR-compliant processing named as a requirement, but this is a growth-stage energy company, not a regulated bank/insurer, placing it at moderate rather than high.
evidence.collaboration_width: Data Engineering; BI; Sales; Marketing; Product; Customer Support
evidence.data_team_maturity: Our stack is in place: BigQuery, dbt, Metabase. What matters now is the layer in between
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: An existing tool stack and data landscape exist but the modeling/governance layer is still being built out, with the JD explicitly framing this as growing and forming rather than fully mature or fully greenfield.
evidence.jd_authorship: You model our data in dbt on BigQuery — from staging through core to the marts — keep the models reliable through tests, reviews and documentation, and keep an eye on run times and cost.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: The JD gives precise, concrete tasks with named tools, layers, and outcome-based milestones (Month 3/6/12) that describe exactly what the person does, a clear hiring-manager voice.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: analysts and business teams can answer their own questions on your models instead of queuing for analytics capacity
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role's primary purpose is building the internal semantic/modeling layer that other data consumers (analysts, BI, business functions) self-serve from.
evidence.autonomy_level: You own the layer between raw data and decisions... you will influence how we model data at RABOT instead of maintaining finished pipelines
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The JD explicitly frames the role as owning and shaping the modeling layer end-to-end rather than executing scoped requests, a strategic autonomy signal repeated throughout.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: No AI coding tool usage or AI-consuming data infrastructure is mentioned anywhere in the JD.
evidence.testing_framing: Core models are covered by tests (uniqueness, freshness, references); errors surface in CI rather than in a management meeting.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Testing, CI, monitoring, and documentation are framed as things the candidate owns and builds as part of their definition of done, not just familiarity with a tool.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: duplicated logic, untested models, expensive queries... Cost per model is transparent, and you have measurably reduced the biggest cost drivers
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: The fear framing centers on unreliable/duplicated models, cost overruns, and firefighting rather than regulatory or compliance risk, placing it at moderate.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: You have named the biggest weaknesses in the existing setup — duplicated logic, untested models, expensive queries — and delivered a prioritised proposal for fixing them.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The role both fixes/cleans up an existing (if immature) stack and builds new shared model infrastructure that doesn't yet exist, a genuinely mixed signal.
evidence.language_gate: English is our working language. German helps with source systems and market documentation, but it is not a requirement.
evidence.loss_aversion: Releases are routine: CI/CD, automated tests and traceable lineage — changes go live without firefighting.
